label: def:categorical-connection
title: Categorical connection and curvature
html:
Definition. Categorical connection and curvature

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum universe over R with differential forms \Omega^k(A) (higher forms).

A categorical connection on A is a morphism \nabla \colon A \to A \otimes \Omega^1(A) in \mathbf{C} satisfying the Leibniz rule \nabla(\mu(a \otimes b)) = \nabla(a) \cdot b + a \cdot \nabla(b). It generalizes the classical de Rham connection d (the \mathrm{SU}(2) instance in Example gives a concrete picture). The rule is expressed by the commutativity of the Leibniz triangle:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:leibniz-triangle}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3.5em]
  A \otimes A
    \ar[r, "\mu"]
    \ar[dr, "{\nabla \otimes 1 + 1 \otimes \nabla}"']
  & A \ar[d, "\nabla"]
  \\
  & A \otimes \Omega^1(A)
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}

The curvature of \nabla is the composition:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:curvature-composition}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=3em]
  A \ar[r, "\nabla"]
  & A \otimes \Omega^1(A) \ar[r, "\nabla"]
  & A \otimes \Omega^2(A)
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}

This composition is denoted F_\nabla = \nabla^2. It is A-linear, a standard consequence of the Leibniz rule.
